questions.questionEn: The guide says Shah Jahan cut off the hands of the Taj Mahal's workers. What do historians say?

options.textEn: It is true, and the workers' names were written in a court diary.
There is no historical evidence for it. It is a popular legend.
Only the chief architect lost his hands, as a punishment.

questions.hintJa: 二度と同じ建物を造らせないために職人の手を切った、という話。記録には残っているだろうか。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 職人の手を切ったという話に、歴史的な裏付けはありません。歴史家たちは、広く語られてきた伝説だと指摘しています。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: この話を裏付ける記録はなく、歴史家は根拠のない伝説としています。建築家だけが罰を受けたという記録もありません。

sources.title: Fact Check: Shah Jahan did not cut off the hands of the masons who constructed the Taj Mahal
sources.claimJa: 職人の手を切ったという話は証拠に裏付けられておらず、ジャワハルラール・ネルー大学の歴史家ナジャフ・ハイダルらも歴史的根拠はないと述べる。

A2.questionEn: A guide says Shah Jahan cut off the workers' hands after they built the Taj Mahal. What do historians say?

options.textEn: It is true. A court diary has the workers' names.
There is no proof. It is an old story that many people tell.
Only the main architect lost his hands. It was a punishment.

B2.questionEn: The guide claims that Shah Jahan had the hands of the Taj Mahal's workers cut off. What is the view of historians?

options.textEn: It is true, and the workers' names were recorded in a court diary.
No historical evidence supports it; it is a widely repeated legend.
Only the chief architect lost his hands, as a form of punishment.

questions.questionEn: Put the two records together. What can you say about the 'Black Taj' across the river?

options.textEn: Black marble from the Taj's garden paths was saved for a second tomb.
The oldest record never calls it black, and the site was a garden for viewing the Taj.
Twenty thousand workers built a black tomb, but the river washed it away.

questions.hintJa: いちばん古い記録に何が書いてあって、何が書いていないか。そして、この岸の土から何が出てきたか。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 黒い墓の話の出どころとされるタヴェルニエの記録は、川の向こうに自分の墓を建て始めたと書くだけで、「黒い」とは書いていません。そして対岸を調べて出てきたのは、タージを眺めるための池のある庭でした。二つを重ねると、「黒いタージ」は記録にも土の中にも見当たらない、と言えます。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 庭の黒い大理石を二つ目の墓に回したという記録も、川が墓を流したという調査結果もありません。タヴェルニエの記録は「黒い」と書かず、対岸から出てきたのはタージを眺めるための池のある庭でした。

sources.publisher: Internet Archive（ジャン＝バティスト・タヴェルニエ『インド旅行記』V・ボール英訳、1889年、第1巻）
sources.title: Travels in India, Vol. 1 (Book I, Chapter VII)
sources.claimJa: タヴェルニエの旅行記は、シャー・ジャハーンが川の向こう岸に自分の墓を建て始めたが息子たちとの戦いで中断したと書き、墓が黒いとは書かない。

sources.title: The Moonlight Garden Reveals New Discoveries at the Taj Mahal
sources.claimJa: インド考古調査局と共同の七年間の調査は、庭がタージとその八角形の池に映る姿を眺めるために設計された可能性が高いとし、黒大理石の墓のための場所という俗説を退けた。

A2.questionEn: Look at the two records together. What can you say about the 'Black Taj' across the river?

options.textEn: They kept black stones from the Taj garden for a second tomb.
The oldest record does not call it black, and the place was a garden to look at the Taj.
Twenty thousand workers built a black tomb, and then the river took it away.

B2.questionEn: Taking both records together, what conclusion can be drawn about the so-called 'Black Taj' across the river?

options.textEn: Black marble from the Taj's garden walkways was being set aside for a second mausoleum.
The earliest account never describes it as black, and the site proved to be a garden for viewing the Taj.
Twenty thousand labourers completed a black tomb, which the river subsequently swept away.

questions.questionEn: After the Taj Mahal was finished, what did many of its skilled builders do next?

options.textEn: They were sent back to Persia and never returned to India.
They stopped working, because nobody needed their skills anymore.
They helped to build Shah Jahan's new capital, Shahjahanabad, in Delhi.

questions.hintJa: シャー・ジャハーンは、タージのあと、デリーに新しい都を築いた。赤い城と大きなモスクのある都だ。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 同じ職人たちが、のちにデリーの新都シャージャハーナーバードの建設に携わったと伝えられています。レッド・フォートやジャーマー・マスジドのある都です。手を切られていたら、できなかった仕事でした。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 職人たちは、のちにデリーの新都シャージャハーナーバードの建設に関わったと伝えられています。技術は途切れず、次の都に受け継がれました。

sources.title: Fact Check: Shah Jahan did not cut off the hands of the masons who constructed the Taj Mahal
sources.claimJa: Times of India（2017年）の報道を引き、同じ職人たちが後にデリーのシャージャハーナーバードを築いたと伝える。

A2.questionEn: Many builders of the Taj Mahal were very good at their work. What did they do after it was finished?

options.textEn: They went back to Persia and never came back to India.
They stopped working. Nobody needed them anymore.
They helped to build Shah Jahan's new capital city, Shahjahanabad, in Delhi.

B2.questionEn: Once the Taj Mahal had been completed, what became of many of the skilled craftsmen who had worked on it?

options.textEn: They were dispatched back to Persia and never returned to India.
They gave up their trade, as their skills were no longer in demand.
They went on to help construct Shah Jahan's new capital, Shahjahanabad, in Delhi.

questions.questionEn: Whose signature can be found among the Taj Mahal's inscriptions?

options.textEn: Shah Jahan's own, carved above the main door.
The calligrapher Amanat Khan's, dated 1638.
The chief stonemason's, carved on Mumtaz's tomb.

questions.hintJa: 壁を飾る美しい文字。それを書いた人だけが、自分の名を残すことを許された。
questions.correctExplanationJa: 廟の内部の銘文を書いた書家アマーナト・ハーン・シーラーズィーは、ヒジュラ暦1048年（1638年）の日付とともに署名を残しました。タージで作品に署名を許されたのは彼だけだったと言われます。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: 署名があるのは書家アマーナト・ハーンです。1638年に内部の銘文を完成させ、自分の名を書き添えました。

sources.title: AMĀNAT KHAN ŠĪRĀZĪ
sources.claimJa: タージ・マハルの大ドーム内の銘文は1048年（1638年）に完成し、書家アマーナト・ハーン・シーラーズィーの署名がある。

sources.title: The calligrapher of Taj Mahal
sources.claimJa: タージ・マハルで自分の作品に署名を許されたのは、アマーナト・ハーンだけだったとされる。

A2.questionEn: One person's name is written among the words on the Taj Mahal's walls. Whose name is it?

options.textEn: Shah Jahan's own name, above the main door.
Amanat Khan's. He was the artist of the writing. It has the year 1638.
The name of the leader of the stone workers, on Mumtaz's tomb.

B2.questionEn: Among all the inscriptions adorning the Taj Mahal, whose signature is to be found?

options.textEn: Shah Jahan's own, carved into the stone above the main entrance.
That of the calligrapher Amanat Khan, bearing the date 1638.
That of the master stonemason, inscribed on Mumtaz's tomb.

questions.questionEn: The guide's family lives in Taj Ganj, just outside the Taj's south gate. What was Taj Ganj in the plan of the Taj Mahal?

options.textEn: A royal hunting ground closed to ordinary people.
A farming village much older than the city of Agra.
A bazaar and caravanserai area that was part of the Taj complex.

questions.hintJa: 墓廟の南門の外には、旅人と商人のための場所が、最初から設けられていた。
questions.correctExplanationJa: タージ・ガンジは、タージ・マハルの南門の外に設けられた市場と隊商宿の区画です。墓廟と同じ計画の一部が、今は人の暮らす町になっています。
questions.incorrectExplanationJa: タージ・ガンジは狩猟場でも古い農村でもなく、南門の外の市場と隊商宿の区画として、タージの複合体の一部でした。

sources.title: Outlying Buildings
sources.claimJa: 南門の外の一段高い場所に、市場と隊商宿の区画であるタージ・ガンジがある。

A2.questionEn: The guide's family lives in Taj Ganj, just outside the south gate of the Taj. What was Taj Ganj in the plan of the Taj Mahal?

options.textEn: A place for the king to hunt. Ordinary people could not go in.
A farm village. It was much older than the city of Agra.
A market area with rooms for travelling traders. It was part of the Taj.

B2.questionEn: The guide's family lives in Taj Ganj, immediately beyond the Taj's southern gate. What role did Taj Ganj play in the original design of the Taj Mahal?

options.textEn: It was a royal hunting reserve from which ordinary people were barred.
It was a farming settlement that long predated the city of Agra.
It was a quarter of bazaars and caravanserais forming part of the Taj complex.
